title: Evaluation-normalized tensor-Hom transport of the boundary pairing
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $i:Z\to T$ a proper morphism of schemes with $T$ quasi-compact, and use the ordinary derived categories, comparison functors $C_W$, exceptional functors $G_e,G_p$, normalized counit and canonical maps $q^e,Q^p$ of [def-weil-boundary-q-maps]. For $W=Z,T$, let $P_W$ be an object predicate on $D(W_e,A)$, fix $\omega_W\in D(W_e,A)$ and $\omega'_W\in D(W_p,A)$, and an isomorphism $w_W:C_W\omega_W\cong\omega'_W$. Write $D_WH=R\mathcal Hom_A(H,\omega_W)$ and $D'_WH'=R\mathcal Hom_A(H',\omega'_W)$ using the ordinary derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Use normalized evaluation and double-dual pairings on both sites [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. For $V\in D(W_e,A)$, an isomorphism $\chi:C_WD_WV\cong D'_WC_WV$ is evaluation-normalized when
$$\chi=R\mathcal Hom_A(C_WV,w_W)\circ a_{V,\omega_W},$$
where $a$ is the evaluation-defined Hom comparison [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison]. For $f:V\otimes_A^LH\to\omega_W$ and $f':C_W(V\otimes_A^LH)\to\omega'_W$, define transpose compatibility to mean
$$\chi\circ C_W(f^\sharp)=(f'\circ c_{W;V,H}^{-1})^\sharp,$$
where $(-)^\sharp$ is the actual tensor-Hom adjunction transpose and $c$ is the canonical monoidal comparison.

Define the duality compatibility property as follows, universally over normalized canonical symmetries, the objects $\omega'_W$, maps $w_W$, normalized pairing witnesses, and isomorphisms $d_e:G_e\omega_T\cong\omega_Z$ and $d_p:G_p\omega'_T\cong\omega'_Z$ satisfying
$$w_Z\circ C_Z(d_e)=d_p\circ G_p(w_T)\circ\theta_{\omega_T}.$$
It requires transpose compatibility for every pairing $f:V\otimes_A^LH\to\omega_Z$ with $P_Z(V),P_Z(H)$, every evaluation-normalized $\chi$, and $f'=w_Z\circ C_Z(f)$; it also requires the evaluation and double-dual comparison property [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] for every $V$ satisfying $P_Z(V)$.

For bounded-below $K,N$ with $e:N\cong D_TK$, require $P_T(K)$, $P_T(N)$, $P_Z(i_e^*K)$, $P_Z(G_eN)$, $P_T(D_TN)$, $P_Z(D_Zi_e^*K)$ and $P_Z(D_ZG_eN)$. Under the counit and projection comparisons and invertibility of the two projection components at $(N,K)$, define the boundary pairing as
$$G_eN\otimes_A^Li_e^*K\xrightarrow{\sigma}i_e^*K\otimes_A^LG_eN\xrightarrow{q^e}G_e(K\otimes_A^LN)\xrightarrow{G_e((\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma)\circ(1\otimes e))}G_e\omega_T\xrightarrow{d_e}\omega_Z.$$
Define its pro-etale counterpart by the identical formula in comparison coordinates: use $Q^p$, the canonical monoidal comparison, $C_T(e)$ followed by evaluation-normalized $\chi_T$, the pro-etale evaluation and signed symmetry, and $d_p$. The property requires transpose compatibility under evaluation-normalized $\chi_Z$ for these pairings, after interchanging their two source factors to place $i_e^*K$ first. Its generic assembly uses supplied functor, Hom-transport, origin-map and counit families; the finite-coefficient specialization supplies exactly the recorded canonical families. The consumer takes $P_W=D^b_{ctf}(W_e,A)$.
